body:
The URL structure of a website influences how search engines understand, index and rank its pages. A clear, descriptive and consistent URL gives both users and Google relevant information about the content of the page before it is even opened.

Although URL structure is not the most important ranking factor, Google has confirmed that URLs are used as a relevance signal.

On a results page where the difference between positions 3 and 5 is minimal, a clear and concise URL can be the factor that attracts the user's click. Long URLs with random parameters and no descriptive words create confusion and reduce the click-through rate in search results.

In this guide you will learn how to create an SEO-optimized URL structure, which mistakes to avoid, how to handle URL changes without losing the traffic you have built up, and how to set up redirects correctly for any later change. This is relevant for any serious long-term SEO optimization strategy.

URL structure and its impact on search engine rankings


A well-thought-out URL structure serves three basic purposes: it helps search engines understand the hierarchy of the website, it gives users clues about the content of the page and it makes it easier to share links online. When a user sees the URL in the address bar, in Google results or shared on social media, it should instantly communicate what the page is about.

Google processes billions of URLs and uses every available signal to assess the relevance and quality of pages. Although keywords in the URL have a more modest impact than the title or the content, they contribute to the overall picture the algorithm forms of a page. A well-structured URL complements the other SEO signals and never contradicts them.

Anatomy of an SEO-optimized URL


A complete URL contains several components, each with a specific role:

https://www.domeniul-dvs.ro/categorie/titlu-pagina/

  • Protocol (https://): HTTPS is mandatory. Google confirms that HTTPS is a ranking signal. Enable the SSL certificate if you have not already done so, because HTTP pages are marked as not secure in modern browsers
  • Domain (www.domeniul-dvs.ro): choose between the www and non-www version and permanently redirect the other one
  • Subdirectory/category (/categorie/): reflects the website hierarchy and the organization of content by topic
  • Page slug (/titlu-pagina/): the most important part, which should contain the main keyword of the page
Each component contributes to the clarity of the URL. The hierarchical structure helps users understand where they are on the website and helps search engines build a correct picture of the site architecture.

Rules for SEO-friendly URLs


Use keywords in the URL


Include the main keyword of the page in the URL, but in a natural and concise way. Compare these examples:
  • Optimal: /optimizare-seo-imagini/
  • Too long: /ghid-complet-optimizare-seo-imagini-wordpress-2026/
  • No keywords: /articol-235/ or /p=1234/
Keywords in the URL have a modest but real impact on rankings. More importantly, they help users understand the content of the page when they see the URL in search results, on social media or in a shared email. A descriptive URL implicitly increases the click-through rate (CTR) compared with a generic URL with numbers or random codes.

Keep URLs short


Short URLs are easier to read, share and remember. Studies of the top 10 Google results show that top URLs have an average of 50-60 characters in the path. Remove connecting words (and, or, of, in, at, for, a, an) that add no semantic value. For example, "ghid-pentru-optimizarea-imaginilor-pe-site" becomes "optimizare-imagini-site" without losing clarity.

Short URLs are more resistant to truncation in interfaces where space is limited: mobile phones, SMS-type messages, tweets or advertising banners. A long URL can be cut off in exactly the wrong place, losing the key information.

Use hyphens between words


Google explicitly recommends using the hyphen (-) as a word separator in URLs. Avoid underscores (_), encoded spaces (%20) or other special characters:
  • Correct: /
  • Incorrect with underscores: /servicii_seo_profesionale/
  • Incorrect with spaces: /servicii%20seo%20profesionale/
Google treats the hyphen as a word separator, which means "servicii-seo" is interpreted as two separate words. The underscore, on the other hand, joins words, so "servicii_seo" is interpreted as a single compound word, reducing relevance for separate search queries.

Use lowercase letters consistently


URLs are case-sensitive on Linux servers. /Pagina/ and /pagina/ are treated as two different URLs, which can cause duplicate content. Use only lowercase letters in URLs and make sure the server automatically redirects any uppercase variant to the lowercase version.

Avoid unnecessary parameters


URLs with multiple parameters (for example: ?id=123&cat=5&ref=google) are hard to read and can cause indexing problems. Every unique combination of parameters generates a new URL, multiplying the number of URLs Googlebot has to process. If parameters are necessary (online store filters, sorting, pagination), set up canonical URLs to tell Google the main version of the page.

URL structure in WordPress


WordPress offers several URL structure options (Permalinks) under Settings, Permalinks. Choosing the right structure from the start is essential, because changing it later affects all existing URLs and requires redirects to be implemented.

The structures recommended for SEO are:

  • Post name (/%postname%/): the most popular and recommended. The URL contains only the post slug: /optimizare-seo/. Simple, clear and easy to manage
  • Category and name (/%category%/%postname%/): adds the category to the URL: /seo/optimizare-seo/. Useful for large websites with many categories and varied content
Avoid structures that include the date (/2026/03/01/titlu/) because they make content look dated and can reduce CTR for evergreen content. An article published in 2020 with the date in the URL will look outdated in 2026, even if the information is up to date.

Whatever structure you choose, make sure it is configured correctly from the very beginning; changing it later requires additional redirect configuration for every existing URL.

Managing URL changes


When you change a URL (changing a slug, restructuring categories, migrating a domain), you must implement 301 redirects so you do not lose the traffic and authority you have built up. A page that has earned external links and Google positions can lose everything if its URL changes without a redirect.

301 redirect (permanent)


A 301 redirect tells Google that the page has moved permanently to a new URL. It passes roughly 90-99% of link authority (link equity) to the new URL. Set up redirects through:
  • The .htaccess file: for Apache servers. It offers granular control and applies immediately
  • cPanel Redirects: from the Domains section of the cPanel panel. A simple visual interface for individual redirects
  • WordPress plugin: Redirection or Yoast SEO Premium handle redirects automatically when a slug changes. Recommended for users without direct server access

302 redirect (temporary)


A 302 redirect is temporary and does not pass link authority. Use it only for temporary situations: pages under construction, seasonal promotions or A/B testing. A common mistake is using 302 redirects instead of 301 for permanent moves, which can lead to the loss of accumulated SEO authority.

404 errors and their SEO impact


When a URL is deleted without a redirect, visitors and search engines get a 404 (Page Not Found) error. 404 pages do not directly affect the ranking of other pages, but the loss of traffic and of the external links that pointed to that URL is a big waste of SEO authority.

Monitor indexing errors in Google Search Console and redirect 404 URLs that have traffic or external links. Check the "Pages", "Not found (404)" section in Search Console to identify all pages with active errors.

Canonical URLs, handling duplicate content


The canonical tag (rel=”canonical”) tells Google which is the main version of a page when several URLs show identical or similar content. Common situations that require a canonical:
  • The www and non-www versions of the same page (/pagina/ accessible on both domain variants)
  • The HTTP and HTTPS versions (if the server does not redirect automatically)
  • Pages with sorting or filtering parameters (online store with ?sort=pret or ?culoare=rosu)
  • Pages accessible through several category paths (/cat1/articol/ and /cat2/articol/)
  • Pagination pages (/categorie/page/2/) versus the main category page
WordPress and Yoast SEO set the canonical tag automatically, but check periodically that it works correctly, especially on online store pages with many filter variations. Any page without an explicit canonical risks competing with duplicate variants of itself.

The impact of URL structure on crawl budget


URLs with multiple parameters and excessive pagination can use up the crawl budget Google allocates to your website. Googlebot spends time crawling URLs with parameters that add no value, at the expense of important pages that should be prioritized.

Practical solutions for optimizing crawl budget:

  • Set URL parameters with no SEO value to "No crawl" in Google Search Console, under Legacy tools, URL parameters
  • Use robots.txt to block access to URLs generated by filters and sorting that you do not want indexed
  • Add noindex to filter pages to prevent them from being indexed and to avoid needlessly using up crawl budget
  • Limit the depth of indexed pagination: /categorie/page/50/ pages have minimal SEO value

Common mistakes in URL structure


Knowing the common mistakes helps you avoid them from the start or identify and fix them on existing websites:
  • Automatically generated URLs with numbers: /post-1234/ gives no information about the content and has a lower CTR than descriptive URLs
  • URLs that are too long: Google may truncate long URLs in search results, reducing visual impact and credibility
  • Changing existing URLs without a redirect: causes 404 errors and the loss of traffic and authority built up over time
  • Inconsistent structures: some pages with a trailing slash (/pagina/) and others without (/pagina) create potential duplicate content problems
  • Special characters and diacritics: avoid ă, î, â, ș, ț and other special characters in URLs. Use the version without diacritics: "ghid-seo" instead of "ghid-seo"
  • Needlessly repeated keywords: /seo/optimizare-seo-seo-ghid/ is over-optimized and can attract penalties

URLs for different page types


The URL strategy must be adapted to the type of page and its goal:

Category and service pages


Category pages benefit from short, direct URLs that contain the main keyword: /servicii-seo/ or /consultanta-seo/. Avoid adding generic words that add no value: /categoria-servicii-de-seo/ is less effective than /servicii-seo/.

Blog articles and guides


Blog articles can have somewhat longer slugs to be descriptive, but keep them under 60 characters. Put the main keyword at the start of the slug for maximum visibility: /audit-securitate-server/ is more effective than /cum-sa-faci-un-audit-de-securitate/.

Product pages in the online store


Product pages benefit from a structure that includes the category and the product name: /electronice/laptop-dell-xps-15/. Avoid including product codes or SKUs in the main URLs; reserve them for canonical URLs or parameters.
URL structure is a decision you make once and that influences the website in the long term. Choose a clear, descriptive and consistent structure from the start to avoid SEO costs later.

URL structure is the technical foundation on which a website's visibility in search engines is built. Solid SEO optimization includes clear URLs, relevant keywords, correct redirects and periodic monitoring of indexing errors to maintain the authority accumulated over time.
